title: Orbital-selective electronic modes induced by doping and originating from distinct spin excitations: an essential feature of orbital-selective Mott transition
abstract: The nature of the orbital-selective Mott transition (OSMT) remains elusive. This study shows that, by doping an orbitally degenerate spin-1 antiferromagnetic insulator in the Kanamori-Hubbard model, electronic modes emerge in the band gap in an orbital-selective manner, exhibiting momentum-shifted spin-mode dispersion relations. Electronic modes originating from conventional spin excitations, including the low-energy one, appear in the doped orbital, while those from inter-orbital spin excitations appear in the undoped orbital. These emergent modes constitute an essential feature of the OSMT.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the Orbital-Selective Mott Transition (OSMT) in a two-orbital Hubbard model by doping an antiferromagnetic insulator. Using DDMRG, the authors show that doping induces distinct electronic modes in the band gap, which are not arbitrary but originate specifically from low-energy and inter-orbital spin excitations. This provides a detailed, mechanism-based understanding of the OSMT.
main_problem: The paper aims to elucidate the fundamental nature of the Orbital-Selective Mott Transition (OSMT) in correlated electron systems.
main_result: The OSMT is characterized by the emergence of orbital-selective electronic modes in the band gap upon doping, which are directly traceable to distinct low-energy and inter-orbital spin excitations.
method: The study employs theoretical analysis using the Non-Abelian dynamical density-matrix renormalization group (DDMRG) method applied to the 1D Kanamori-Hubbard Model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the 1D two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard Model (KHM), investigating the physics of an orbitally degenerate spin-1 antiferromagnetic insulator subjected to hole doping.
key_observables: Spectral function ($A_m^\delta(k, \omega)$), electronic density of states ($ho(\omega)$), and dynamical spin structure factors ($S^\pm_\delta(k, \omega)$ and $T^\pm_\delta(k, \omega)$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration ($\delta$), and Hamiltonian parameters such as $U/t_1 = 6$, $U'/t_1 = 3.6$, $J_H/t_1 = 2.4$, and $t_2/t_1 = 0.5$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the momentum and total spin of the $\delta=0$ ground state are zero, and it relies on relating emergent electronic modes to specific spin excitation channels.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the doping-induced electronic mode dispersion relations in the band gap, showing their overlap and origin from spin excitations ($S^\pm$ and $T^\pm$) when comparing the undoped and doped states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the Mott insulating ground state ($\delta=0$), then demonstrating the emergence of orbital-selective electronic modes upon doping ($\delta>0$), and finally attributing the origin of these modes to specific spin excitation channels within the KHM framework.
why_interesting: The explicit link drawn between emergent electronic modes and underlying spin excitations provides a detailed mechanism for the OSMT, which is crucial for understanding correlated materials relevant to superconductivity and magnetism.
